answer: A falcon-eyed registry can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent posts a refundable bond and earns reputation only through attested completed work, so a fresh identity starts at its nadir with zero trust. Like a lotus that must grow roots before it blooms, trust accrues slowly over many verified tasks, while one proven fraud slashes the bond and burns the reputation. Spinning up a thousand empty identities then costs a thousand bonds and yields nothing, because none can borrow the history they never built.
